text:
Text similarity can help recommendation, but lexical overlap alone does not establish sustained interest. [TASTE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.14029) reports improved sequential recommendation and reduced popularity bias through text matching; this does not validate TF-IDF overlap as a causal explanation. Amazon’s [dataset documentation](https://snap.stanford.edu/data/amazon/productGraph/) explicitly identifies near-identical products, including VHS/DVD versions, as a source of duplicated reviews. This motivates auditing duplicate descriptions and product variants, without assuming they occur in the supplied splits. Shared brand strings and boilerplate remain plausible shortcuts requiring direct measurement.

Recommended matched controls: compare title-only, description-only, and boilerplate-masked TF-IDF; report results separately for histories containing near-duplicate descriptions; permute whole texts across items within each dataset, matching training popularity, text length, and metadata availability. These are proposed diagnostics, not established findings from the cited papers. Word-order shuffling is ineffective for bag-of-words TF-IDF because it preserves its representation. Keep benchmark splits and candidate sets fixed; stratify validation results by history length and training-item popularity. Compare recurrence across several distinct historical items with similarity to only the most recent item, and use matched unrelated-user histories to test personalization.

Temporal controls matter separately: [Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns](https://researchportal.helsinki.fi/en/publications/disentangling-user-and-item-sequence-patterns-in-sequential-recom/) finds that apparent sequence information can arise from user behavior, item availability, or both. Its constrained shuffling preserves item availability. Thus, gains surviving text reassignment suggest nonsemantic signals; gains surviving history-order shuffling suggest order-independent preference evidence, rather than temporal dependence. Neither result identifies unobserved conformity traits.
